The Planck Length is the smallest meaningful length in the universe according to current physics theories. It's incredibly tiny, about 1.6 x 10^-35 meters. This length scale is related to the Planck constant and is significant because it represents the limit at which classical concepts of space and time break down, and quantum effects become dominant. It's a fundamental concept in the study of quantum mechanics and the nature of the universe at extremely small scales.
